newsitem.title: CONGO: Agip unit to rebuild Congo link to Cabinda.
newsitem.headline: Agip unit to rebuild Congo link to Cabinda.

text.p: Oil company Agip-Recherches-Congo is providing four billion CFA francs ($7.0 million) to rebuild a road from Congo's business capital, Pointe Noire, to the border with Angola's Cabinda province in the southwest, Congo government sources said on Thursday.
The work on the 35 km road will take 12 months and is part of a government programme to upgrade the country's road network. Only 1,300 kms of the country's 17,850 kms of roads are tarmac.
The rebuilding of this road is expected to improve trade between the south of Congo, the northwest of Zaire and the Angolan enclave of Cabinda squeezed between them.
Agip-Recherches-Congo is a 100-percent-owned unit of Agip of Italy.
